property_summary: If withdrawAll(msg.sender) reverts when called by some address, then it must revert when called by any different caller (i.e., only the owner can successfully call withdrawAll).

For any recipient address and any funded contract balance, when the caller is the owner, withdrawAll(address) transfers the full contract balance to the provided _recipient (so address(_recipient).balance increases by the withdrawn amount); the mutant breaks this by always sending to owner instead of the provided recipient.

For any recipient address and any funded contract balance, when the caller is owner the reference contract sends the contract balance to the provided recipient (so address(recipient).balance increases by that amount); the mutant instead always sends to owner, violating this for some recipient ≠ owner.

For any nonzero contract balance and any recipient address, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's balance becomes zero (funds are forwarded to the recipient); the mutant sending instead always to owner can leave the recipient's balance unchanged (and still zero contract balance) but the distinguishing universal property is: after owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the contract balance is zero and the recipient's balance increases by the withdrawn amount whenever recipient != owner — the mutant violates this for some recipient != owner by sending to owner instead.

For every nonzero contract balance and for every recipient address that is a contract which REVERTS on receiving Ether, the reference C will forward funds to that recipient (causing withdrawAll to revert when recipient rejects receipt), whereas the mutant that always pays owner will not attempt to send to the provided recipient and so will NOT revert for some inputs where recipient != owner; thus the general rule: if the recipient contract reverts on receive, withdrawAll(revertingRecipient) called by owner reverts on the reference but succeeds on the mutant.

For every recipient address R and any funded contract balance, when the owner calls withdrawAll(R) the reference contract transfers the contract balance to R (so address(R).balance increases by that amount) — therefore if R is a contract that records incoming payments (increments a public counter) the reference causes that counter to increase but the mutant that always pays owner will not increase R's counter for some R != owner.
After owner calls withdrawAll, the balance of contract C becomes zero.
If the caller is not the contract owner, withdrawAll must revert (reverted == true); otherwise it may not revert.
If caller is not the owner known via the public getter, the call to withdrawAll must revert (i.e., (caller != owner) == reverted).
If caller is not the owner known via the public getter, the call to withdrawAll must revert (i.e., (caller != owner) == reverted).
If caller is not the owner known via the public getter, the call to withdrawAll must revert (i.e., (caller != owner) == reverted).

For any recipient address and any initial contract balance funded by the owner caller, calling withdrawAll transfers the entire contract balance out (address(c).balance == 0 afterwards); the mutant that calls transfer(0) leaves nonzero balance for some inputs and thus violates this.

For any caller who is the owner and any recipient address, after calling withdrawAll with Ether deposited in the contract, the reference contract transfers the entire contract balance (address(c).balance == 0), whereas the mutant that calls transfer(0) can leave a nonzero balance; the test fuzzes recipient and deposit amount and asserts that address(c).balance == 0 after withdrawAll.

For any owner caller and any nonzero ETH deposit held by the contract, calling withdrawAll(recipient) empties the contract (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that calls transfer(0) can leave a nonzero balance and thus violates this.

For any owner caller and any recipient that is a contract whose fallback/receive reverts on receiving ETH, withdrawAll(recipient) always leaves C's balance as 0 (reference forwards funds and will revert the whole call if transfer fails), whereas the mutant that transfers 0 will leave the contract balance unchanged (nonzero) for some inputs.

For any owner caller and any nonzero deposit, calling withdrawAll(recipient) transfers exactly the contract balance to the recipient so that the contract's balance becomes zero (the mutant that transfers 0 leaves a nonzero balance for some deposits/recipients), therefore address(c).balance == 0 after a successful owner withdrawAll call.

After the owner funds the contract and calls withdrawAll, the recipient receives the entire contract balance (i.e. address(c).balance becomes 0 and recipient's balance increases by the full prior contract balance).

If the caller passed to the test is not c.owner(), then the withdrawAll call reverted.
After a caller who is the owner invokes withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's owner remains equal to the caller.
